title: A proof reads a few stored hash tiles and never a leaf, from the first request after a start
purpose: Tom's rule: a start never reads the whole history, and nothing on a first request does either. Today a frontier log starts from its snapshot and reads only the tail, but the first inclusion proof after every start builds the whole proof tree by reading every stored leaf (crates/lys-log-store/src/frontier_log.rs, proof_tree at line 323, the loop at line 329). The receipts route asks for one (crates/lys-identity-server/src/receipts_api.rs line 45, through crates/lys-identity/src/restart.rs line 382), and so does a certificate's proof (crates/lys-identity-server/src/certificates_store.rs line 310). So the first receipt after each restart of the installed service reads the whole log, and the tree it builds is then held in memory at a size that grows with the log.
task: Store the log's hashes as C2SP tlog-tiles beside its leaves, written by every append before the pin, and build every inclusion and consistency proof from the few tiles it needs. Remove the whole-log proof tree from the frontier log. Give a log made before tiles its tiles once, and prove by test that neither a start nor a first proof reads a leaf before the tail.

requirements.title: Every append writes its hashes into tiles before the pin
requirements.spec: Behavioural. A store that serves proofs also stores hash tiles in the C2SP tlog-tiles layout under its directory: tile/<L>/<N> holds 256 hashes of level L (level 0 holds leaf hashes, level L+1 holds the hash of each full tile of level L), and a tile not yet full is kept as tile/<L>/<N>.p/<W>, holding its W hashes. The tile paths follow the specification's encoding of N. A new trait in crates/lys-log-store, beside LeafStore, carries the reading and writing of one tile; FileLeafStore implements it with the same durability as a leaf (a temporary name, flushed, renamed, the directory flushed), and each store in the tests implements it in memory. FrontierLog::append writes the leaf hash it already computes into the level-0 tile, and every higher tile the append completes, before it moves the pin. So every leaf under the pin has its hashes in tiles. A partial tile made stale by a longer one is removed only after the longer one is durable. The layout is local state, as the leaves are, and the module documentation says so.
acceptance: After appends of 1, 255, 256, 257, 65,535, 65,536 and 65,537 leaves, every stored tile equals the hashes an independent Merkle computation gives for its range (lys-core's HashTree over the same leaves), and every full tile is exactly 8,192 bytes.
A test that fails the tile write makes the append fail with the tile's path named, and the pin does not move.
A test that stops after the leaf and before its tile, then reopens, finds the leaf in the tail and its hash written into the tile by the open, which reads no leaf before the tail.

requirements.title: Proofs are built from the tiles they need
requirements.spec: Behavioural. FrontierLog answers an inclusion proof for index i in tree size n, and a consistency proof from size m to n, by reading only the tiles that hold the proof's hashes: each hash in a proof is the hash of a whole subtree, read as one entry of a tile, or hashed from the entries of one tile when the subtree is smaller than a tile or runs into the partial right edge. proof_tree and the OnceLock<HashTree> it fills are removed, so the log holds no structure whose size grows with the log. restart.rs inclusion_proof and certificates_store.rs prove call the new methods. lys-core's HashTree stays for the callers that build a tree from leaves they already hold.
acceptance: For every tree size from 1 to 600 and every index in it, and for 2^16 + 3 leaves at 50 indices across the tree, the inclusion proof from tiles equals lys-core's HashTree proof, and so does the consistency proof for every m below n in the first range.
In a log of 1,048,576 leaves, a counting store shows an inclusion proof reads no leaf and no more than 16 tiles, and a consistency proof no more than 32.
A tile that is missing or whose bytes do not rebuild the pinned root is refused tile_mismatch naming its path, and no proof is answered from it.

requirements.title: A log made before tiles gets them once
requirements.spec: Behavioural. A store that has leaves under its pin and no tiles is given its tiles once, when the frontier log first opens it under this build: every pinned leaf is read once, one at a time, its hash written into the tiles, and the tiles are checked against the pinned root before the open answers. The start says it by name, as tiles built from N leaves. A store whose tiles cover its pin is never given them again. This is the one read of every leaf this card allows, once per log, like the first pin of an unpinned requests log (crates/lys-identity-server/src/requests_state.rs line 99). A store whose tiles are partly present, or do not rebuild the pinned root, is refused tile_mismatch by name; the fix the refusal names is to remove the tile folder so the tiles are made again.
acceptance: A log written by the build before this card, of 10,000 leaves, opens once with its tiles built, and a second open reads no leaf before the tail.
The line the start prints names that tiles were built and from how many leaves.
A tile folder cut off in the middle is refused tile_mismatch at open, naming the tile, and nothing is appended.

requirements.title: A gate test fails when a start or its first proof reads past the tail
requirements.spec: Behavioural. A test in the log store and one in the service drive a start and then the first proof over a store that counts the leaves it reads, and fail when either reads a leaf before the tail. The service test runs the receipts route: it appends 5,000 events, restarts the service over the same directory, asks for a receipt of an early event, and checks the answer verifies and that no leaf before the tail was read. Both run in the full Lys gate.
acceptance: Run against main before this card, the log store test fails naming the leaves read, and the service test fails the same way.
At the card's head both pass inside the full Lys gate.

boundaries: SHALL NOT read a leaf before the tail on a start or on any proof, apart from R3's one adoption per log.
SHALL NOT hold in memory any structure whose size grows with the log.
SHALL NOT change what a leaf holds, how a leaf is named, or what the pin or the snapshot means.
SHALL NOT add a timeout, deadline, sleep, poll interval, #[allow], #[ignore], unsafe code or any bypass.
SHALL NOT add a silent fallback: a missing or wrong tile is a named refusal, never a quiet rebuild.
verification: The full Lys gate, the ast-grep scan and the file-length check exit 0 at the card's head, measured by the card round.
On a scratch install with a few thousand directory events: restart the service and ask for a receipt; the start line and a count of leaf reads show no leaf before the tail was read.
